title: Hosted API: token directionality reconciliation and minimums experiment (session-aware billing probe)
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Run a controlled experiment to evaluate a session-aware, directionally-weighted billing model for the Hosted API that reconciles input/output token rates for streaming calls, introduces an optional session minimum (time-windowed), and measures customer retention and enterprise SQ friction. The goal is to find a pricing construct that better aligns cost-to-serve with observable server load while minimizing commercial friction for enterprise legal/SQ responses.
background: Current hosted token billing treats input and output tokens with a fixed ratio in select proposals, and many pilot tickets have explored asymmetric floors and streaming minimums. Enterprise customers have raised two recurring asks: (1) predictable minimums tied to active sessions instead of per-minute streaming metering, and (2) transparent mapping between protocol-level directionality (ingress vs egress) and invoice line items to satisfy security questionnaire disclosures. Recent telemetry shows significant variance in per-session egress:ingress ratios across workloads (chat assistants vs retrieval-augmented tasks). We need an experiment that tests session-aware minimums and a reconciliation method that reduces billing noise for customers while reflecting actual cost variance.
hypothesis: A session-aware minimum applied at the session/window level (e.g., per 10-minute active window) combined with a small egress-premium multiplier for streaming sessions will: (a) reduce billing disputes by 30% for pilot enterprises, (b) maintain or improve usage retention for high-throughput customers, and (c) recover ~8-12% of cost delta observed from asymmetric egress-heavy workloads compared to flat symmetric pricing.
experiment_design: 1) Create a gating flag 'session_meter_v2' in billing service (ENG-33210) that records session start/end and active windows. 2) Define a 10-minute active-window minimum of 250 tokens (configurable per account) that is applied once per window if total tokens < minimum. 3) Apply directional weighting: egress tokens billed at 1.15x, ingress at 1.0x for streaming sessions in the experiment cohort. 4) Run A/B cohorts: control (current symmetric token pricing) vs variant A (session minimum only) vs variant B (session minimum + egress premium). 5) Enroll 50 mid-size customers and 10 enterprise trial accounts with opt-in consent; pilot duration 6 weeks. 6) Instrument billing reconciliation logs and SQ artifact generation to capture directionality breakdowns on invoices and to produce pre-filled SQ snippets for customers.
success_criteria: net revenue delta within expected recovery band (8%-12%) without >5% usage churn
SQ intake time for enterprise decrease by 15% due to pre-filled directionality artifacts
no customer-facing latency regressions attributable to metering instrumentation
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Engineering implements feature flag and logs (ENG-33210) and provides test harness. Phase 1 (2 weeks): Internal QA and opt-in sandbox with 5 trusted customers (observability + invoice preview). Phase 2 (6 weeks): Run A/B experiment across enrolled customers; product and finance monitor telemetry weekly. Phase 3: Evaluate results with legal and sales; prepare commercial playbook and optional per-account configuration UI in Console. If successful, graduate to wider beta and prepare quota/pricing doc updates.
risks: enterprises surprise at appearance of separate egress line items causing procurement pushback
edge-case workloads (high-frequency tiny messages) may hit minimums and experience large effective per-token price increases
billing pipeline performance impact from additional session bookkeeping
legal/SQ templates may require multiple iterations to satisfy large regulated customers
mitigation: pre-engage top 5 pilot accounts via solutions engineering to co-design minimums and thresholds
provide a cost simulator in Console so customers can preview billing impact by workload
limit initial cohort size, feature-flagged and opt-in; monitor billing pipeline resource usage and scale infra (ENG-33890)
prepare customer-facing collateral and draft SQ snippets for security review prior to rollout
